TutorContacts supports these everyday contact-management tasks:
* add, list, view, edit, and delete student and parent contacts;
* link parents to students and remove links when arrangements change;
* find contacts by name, filter by name, subject, or level, and sort by academic level;
* use notes and tags to keep useful context; and
* save data locally between sessions, with a single-instance lock to prevent conflicting writes.

The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T17-1/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T17-1/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.

Before initializing `Storage`, `MainApp` acquires an exclusive operating-system lock on `.tutorcontacts.lock` in the
application home. `ApplicationLock` holds the lock for the process lifetime. A second instance using the same home
shows an error and exits before reading or writing contacts or preferences. The zero-byte lock file may remain after
exit; only the held operating-system lock indicates a running instance, so a crash does not leave a stale reservation.

**Representation.** `AddressBook` keeps a list of `ParentStudentLink` objects beside its `UniquePersonList`.
Each link identifies its parent and its student by `Name` and `Phone`, compared in the same normalized way as the
also check the contact's `Role`, because a parent and a student may share a name and phone. Within one role, name
and phone identify at most one contact, so each link resolves to exactly one parent and one student.
A parent can have 0..* linked students and a student can have 0..* linked parents.
The detail pane and `link` messages show each linked contact as `Name (phone)`, distinguishing shared names.
**Normal path.** `LinkCommandParser` parses two displayed-list indices with `ParserUtil#parseTwoDisplayedIndices`.
`LinkCommand` and `UnlinkCommand` both extend `ParentStudentCommand`, whose `getParentAndStudent` looks up both
contacts in `Model#getFilteredPersonList()`, then rejects the same index twice, then checks that the first contact
is a parent and the second a student. Looking up both contacts first means an index outside the list is reported even
when both indices are equal. `LinkCommand#execute` creates the link with `ParentStudentLink#between`, rejects a
duplicate using `Model#hasLink`, calls `Model#addLink`, and returns a result that selects the parent and displays its
details. `LogicManager` saves the address book because the command changes data. `PersonListPanel` asks
`Logic#getLinkedPersons` for the selected contact's linked contacts and shows them in `ContactDetailPanel`.
**Removing a link.** `UnlinkCommand` runs the same checks, then requires the link to exist (`Model#hasLink`) and calls
`Model#removeLink`, which asserts that the link exists and removes only that link. Both contacts and their other links
are kept, and the parent is selected so its remaining links appear in the detail pane. Sharing the checks in
`ParentStudentCommand`, and the index parsing in `ParserUtil`, keeps the two commands' validation and messages
**Keeping links consistent.** `AddressBook` updates links whenever contacts change, so every command that changes
contacts keeps links valid without extra code:
* `removePerson` removes every link that involves the deleted contact. `DeleteCommand` reports how many it removed.
* `setPerson` calls `ParentStudentLink#withContactReplaced`, which rewrites the side of a link that matched the
edited contact. Editing a name or phone therefore keeps the link.
* `resetData` replaces contacts and links together. `clear` supplies an empty address book, removing both;
save-failure rollback supplies the previous snapshot, restoring both.
**Storage.** `JsonSerializableAddressBook` saves links in a `links` list of `JsonAdaptedLink` objects, each holding the
two names and phones as strings. When loading, it rejects a link with invalid fields, a link whose parent or student
is not in the `persons` list, and a duplicate link, so a corrupted file is reported instead of loading broken links.
A file without a `links` list loads with no links, so data files from earlier versions remain valid.

* Pros: `Person` and its equality are unchanged, deleting and editing update links in one place, and the data file

* Cons: a link must be rewritten when a linked contact's name or phone changes.
* **Alternative 2:** store a list of linked students inside each parent `Person`.
* Pros: a card can read links straight from its contact.
* Cons: every `Person` copy (for example in `edit`) must carry the links, and deleting a student must update every
* **Alternative 3:** give each `Person` a generated ID and link by ID.
* Pros: links survive any edit without rewriting.
* Cons: IDs must be generated, saved, and validated, which adds risk to every existing command and data file.
**Target user profile**: An independent private tutor who manages approximately 15–30 students and their parents,
works alone, and prefers typing commands to navigating menus. The tutor needs to retrieve contact and tutoring
information while preparing lessons or communicating with parents.
**Value proposition**: TutorContacts keeps student and parent contact information, together with essential tutoring
details, in one place. Typed commands let the tutor record contacts and retrieve the information needed for lesson
preparation or parent communication. The initial MVP focuses on creating, viewing, deleting, and retaining contact
records. Version 1.4 adds parent-student links so the tutor can see which parents belong to which students.
Version 1.5 adds unlinking, filtering, level sorting, a persistent detail pane, and protection against two
running copies overwriting each other's data.

The add parser accepts `r/`, `n/`, `p/`, `e/`, `a/`, `s/`, `l/`, and `o/`. All are single-value prefixes.
Unknown-prefix detection runs before duplicate-prefix detection, followed by base-field presence, role,
role-specific field rules, field-value validation, and model duplicate detection. `Subject`, `Level`, and `Note`
reuse the model/storage foundation; `Person` retains its compatibility constructor for legacy records.
Newly added students must have subject and level, while parents cannot supply either prefix.
Field constructors normalize values and share validation with `ParserUtil` and JSON loading. Names are
compared case-insensitively for duplicate identity; capitalization remains significant for full object equality
and is retained in stored data. `ExitCommandParser` rejects arguments before an exit result can reach the UI.
`Email` uses possessive repetition for the dot-separated domain labels. A label cannot contain a dot, so consumed
labels do not need to be reconsidered. This avoids recursive matcher backtracking for long domains while retaining
the existing email grammar and shared command/JSON validation. No email-length limit is introduced.
`Address` retains `String.trim()` normalization and the 1–150 code-point limit. Its regex requires at least one character
in Unicode category `L`, `N`, `P`, or `S`, and still excludes controls (`Cc`) and line/paragraph separators (`Zl`, `Zp`).
Formatting and combining marks are preserved alongside qualifying content. Values containing only spaces, formatting,
or marks are rejected through both command parsing and JSON loading. This is a category-based policy: the letter
U+3164 and symbol U+2800 satisfy it even when their rendering appears blank. Do not describe the rule as detecting
every visually invisible value. A newly invalid stored address triggers the existing startup warning and write
protection; users repair the preserved file before restarting. No address or contact is silently substituted or dropped.
`AddressBookParser` strips outer command padding with `String.strip()`. `ListCommandParser` uses `isBlank()`, and
`SortCommandParser` strips its criterion before comparing it with `level`. These methods use Java whitespace,
including U+2003 EM SPACE; U+00A0 NON-BREAKING SPACE and U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE are not Java whitespace. Prefix
recognition and separators inside commands retain their existing syntax.
`ParserUtil.parseNote` treats empty or Java-whitespace-only input as absent. `Note` strips surrounding Java
whitespace before validating length and content, while preserving internal spacing. `JsonAdaptedPerson` also maps
missing, empty, or Java-whitespace-only stored notes to absence, keeping files saved by earlier versions loadable.

**Difficulty.** AB3 manages one kind of entity with independent records. TutorContacts manages two roles with
different rules (students need a subject and academic level, parents cannot have them) and relationships between
contacts (parent-student links), while keeping AB3's guarantees: every command is typed, every change is saved, and
the data file stays editable by hand.
* **Role-specific contacts.** Adding roles touched parsing, validation, duplicate detection, display, storage, and
editing. Older data files without a subject or level still had to load and stay editable.
* **Parent-student links.** Links identify contacts by normalized name and phone instead of generated IDs, so the data
file stays readable. In exchange, every change to contacts (edit, delete, clear, and the rollback after a failed
save) must keep links valid, and loading must reject links to missing contacts or duplicates. Linking and unlinking
share one validation path, so both report the same problems in the same order.
* **Filtering and sorting the displayed list.** `filter`, `find`, and `sort` change what is displayed but not what is
stored. Every index-based command, the selected contact shown in the detail pane, and the effect of `add`, `edit`,
and `list` had to stay consistent with the displayed order.
* **Safe data handling.** Saves replace the data file atomically, a failed save rolls back the in-memory change, an
invalid or unreadable file is reported without being overwritten, and application files stay beside the JAR.
Validation handles Unicode whitespace, escaped prefix-shaped text, and very long input without crashing.

27 October (RepoSense code dashboard), and the test suite has grown to about 580 tests, including desktop UI tests.

### Adding a student or parent contact: `add`
Adds a student or parent contact to TutorContacts.
Format: `add r/ROLE n/NAME p/PHONE e/EMAIL a/ADDRESS [s/SUBJECT] [l/LEVEL] [o/NOTE]`
* `ROLE` must be `student` or `parent` and is case-insensitive.
* Role, name, phone, email, and address are required. Parameters may appear in any order.
* Students must supply one subject with `s/` and one academic level with `l/`. Otherwise, TutorContacts reports
`Student contacts require both s/SUBJECT and l/LEVEL.`
* Parents must omit both `s/` and `l/`; even empty versions of these prefixes are rejected with
`Subject and level are only valid for student contacts.`
![Error shown when a parent contact is given a subject](images/addParentWithSubjectError.png)
* Either role may supply `o/NOTE`. An omitted or whitespace-only note is treated as absent.
* `t/` and other unsupported prefixes are rejected. Adding tags or multiple subjects is not supported.
* On success, TutorContacts reports `Added student: NAME.` or `Added parent: NAME.`
* The newly added contact is selected and scrolled into view; its complete information appears in the detail pane.
Field rules apply to normalized values. Leading and trailing spaces and tabs are trimmed; consecutive spaces in
names, subjects, and levels are collapsed. Capitalization is retained except for roles and academic levels,
which are stored in their canonical forms.
| Role | `student` or `parent`, ignoring case; stored in lowercase. |

| Name | 1–70 characters; starts with a letter or digit; letters (including accented letters and other scripts' vowel signs and marks), digits, spaces, straight apostrophes (`'`), full stops, and hyphens. Replace a curly apostrophe (`’`) with `'`. Slashes are not allowed, even with a [backslash escape](#prefixes-and-literal-text), so write a patronymic such as `s/o` or `d/o` as `s.o.` or `d.o.`, for example `n/Ravi s.o. Kumar`. |
| Phone | 3–15 digits; optional leading `+`; spaces and hyphens only between digits. |
| Email | One `@`, a nonempty local part, and at least two nonempty dot-separated domain labels. No internal whitespace; domain labels use letters, digits, and internal hyphens. |
| Address | 1–150 characters on one line; no control characters; must include a Unicode letter, number, punctuation mark, or symbol. |
| Subject | 1–40 characters; letters, digits, spaces, and `& + - ' / ( ) . ,`. |
| Level | `Primary 1`–`Primary 6`, `Secondary 1`–`Secondary 5`, or `JC 1`–`JC 2`. Input is case-insensitive and stored as, for example, `Secondary 3` or `JC 2`. |
| Note | 1–200 printable characters on one line, or empty to omit it. |
Addresses retain the existing trimming of leading and trailing characters at or below U+0020, including ordinary spaces
and tabs. The length limit counts Unicode code points, including accompanying combining marks.
Other Unicode spaces, format characters, and combining marks can accompany address content, but cannot
satisfy the required content rule alone. For example, an address containing only ZERO WIDTH SPACE (U+200B),
NON-BREAKING SPACE (U+00A0), or combining accents is rejected. Ordinary Unicode text and its accompanying marks or
This rule uses Unicode categories: BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK (U+2800) counts as a symbol and HANGUL FILLER (U+3164)
counts as a letter, even when they appear blank in a font.
Notes also trim surrounding Java whitespace, including EN SPACE (U+2002), EM SPACE (U+2003), and IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE
(U+3000), before checking the 200-character limit. Internal spacing in a nonblank note is preserved. A note containing
only Java whitespace is absent on add and cleared on edit. NON-BREAKING SPACE (U+00A0) and ZERO WIDTH SPACE (U+200B)
are retained as note content; they do not clear a note.
`JC 5`, `Secondary 6`, `Primary 7`, abbreviations such as `P6`, and custom labels such as `Adult` are
rejected. The error is `Level must be Primary 1-6, Secondary 1-5, or JC 1-2 (for example, Secondary 3).`
The same rules apply to level values in JSON. Unsupported values make the file invalid and trigger
